clue.text: Realise son needs hospital after return of skin disease

indicators.note: after places the son and hospital letters behind the turned disease
a return is a going back, so the skin disease is read from its end to its start

parts.note: acne is a common skin disease
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient's skin complaint has come back and their son needs a hospital visit.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to convert it into cash, the same sense of cashing in.

clue.text: Delete parts of folder, as example?

indicators.note: the answer is made of parts of these words, sitting across their joins

explanation.surface: Asks whether wiping a computer folder is an example of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across foldER AS Example.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to delete text or a file is to wipe it out completely.

clue.text: Shortly phone agent about love ballad

love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A quick phone call to an agent about a love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' trims CALL to CAL; 'about' turns SPY into YPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean song form, often topical and witty, so loosely a kind of ballad or song.

clue.text: Wild tiger seen here in Africa?

indicators.note: wild letters are untamed and run loose, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Suggests that a tiger in the wild might be spotted somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that tigers are Asian: you would not see one on this African plain, though wild animals of other kinds abound there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tanzanian national park is a place in Africa where wild animals are seen, the place 'here' points to.

clue.text: A standard to meet for ancient believer

to see someone is to meet them

explanation.definitionFit: A Zoroastrian of India, follower of the ancient Persian religion, so a believer in an ancient faith.

clue.text: Quick answer reflected ill

parts.note: ill as a noun means harm or evil

explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns EVIL into LIVE. 'Quick' is the old sense, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic sense of quick is living, surviving in phrases like cut to the quick.

clue.text: Special person lamenting footballer

parts.note: someone lamenting cries, so is a weeper

explanation.surface: A particular person mourning a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: In football this is a defensive player positioned behind the back line, so an example of a footballer.

clue.text: "Unexpected item in bagging area" keeps good customers primarily puzzling

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the good letter goes within
unexpected things turn up out of order, so these letters are rearranged
bagging means taking into the bag, so the area letter joins the letters being rearranged
primarily picks the first letter of the word customers

explanation.surface: The infamous self-checkout announcement baffles shoppers, mostly the good customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagging' takes A in with ITEM IN and 'Unexpected' rearranges them to ENIMATI; 'keeps' then holds G inside, and C comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enigmatic is mysterious and hard to understand, so puzzling.

clue.text: For one, Tate & Lyle sugar sadly lacks American backing

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lacks means is without, so these letters are taken out
backing means going in reverse, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A sad tale of a sugar brand going short of American financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns US into SU, which 'lacks' takes from LYLESUGAR, leaving LYLEGAR for 'sadly' to rearrange. Tate & Lyle is a British sugar company.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate in London is an art gallery, so it is one example.

clue.text: Priest feeds dog? That's 15's work!

Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

clue.text: A small quantity from factory I spread around

parts.note: marg, short for margarine, is a spread for bread

explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns MARG into GRAM. Marg is British shorthand for margarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousandth of a gram is a tiny measure of weight, so a small quantity.

clue.text: Answering mobile in vespers embodies oafishness, for a start

mobile means able to move, so these letters are moved about
for a start takes the first letter of oafishness

explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges IN VESPERS and 'embodies' puts O within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being responsive means reacting or replying, the sense of answering.

clue.text: Crowd drifted back to front

parts.note: to rove is to wander or drift

explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the final D of ROVED to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a moving crowd or herd, people or animals in numbers.

clue.text: Lovely old home? Not true

a nest is a home

clue.text: Deliberately mislead about book's cost to deliver

B is the abbreviation for book; the 's is just possessive
a rate is a cost or charge

clue.text: Busy person by hot stove grabs time for 90s comedy film

indicators.note: grabs means takes hold of, so the time letter is held inside

parts.note: busy as a bee, so a busy person is a bee
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an oven is a stove

clue.text: Drug's finally looking hopeful

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of looking

clue.text: To be left in the lurch at heart upset nursing unit

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the unit letter sits within
upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged
at heart takes the central letter of lurch

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, a unit

explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' gives R from LURCH; 'upset' rearranges THE + R into HERT, and 'nursing' puts I inside to give HERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive a bequest, which is to be left something in a will.

clue.text: And this for Caesar is a moral code

hic is Latin for this, again in Caesar's language

explanation.walkthrough: 'for Caesar' says both words are Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles, a moral code.

clue.text: Century of barbarian terror one overlooked

A is one, as the indefinite article

clue.text: Why ark isn't shark food?

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a riddle: ark is shark with no SH, and NO SH, run together, is slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for grub or a meal.

clue.text: Try to keep nut he'd pickled? He would
